submission.natural_language_explanation: Dense broad previous-token head: at each measured position it attends almost entirely to the immediately preceding token (0.94-1.00 at peaks) and its strength is how far that token's value sits from the head's mean write, so it sits active-weak on most ordinary prose of 8+ tokens (peaks ~0.9-2.1, straddling the 0.25x line) and fires strongly (1.5-4.2) on the second and later pieces of a tokenizer-split word or name (Mc|Pherson, Sch|oen, Mc|Intosh, un|prosperous, ä|u, сп|и, U|.|S, there|'s), on 'is/are' directly after sentence-initial 'There', and on rare content-word pairings (fish|swam, open|wide, stops|there, The|up). It stays below the line only on (a) a one-word text of a single vocabulary token plus '.' (Water., Sorry., True., Hello., Yes.) and (b) short 3-7-token 'The'-opened clauses built only from top-common single-token nouns, light verbs and prepositions (The dog ran, The cat sat, The bird sang/flew, The man walked, The child laughed, The baby cried, The house is near the park, The dog bit the man, The cat chased the mouse); any proper name, split word, numeral, there/here/where, 'and'/comma, adjective, or uncommon pairing (swam, barked, won, wide, door, up) in the same frame pushes it over the line.

rival_explanations: The head is a generic bigram-surprisal detector with no special status for tokenization: any rare adjacent pairing fires equally, so split-words, There+be and rare bigrams like fish|swam are one class and single-token rare pairs (e.g. an uncommon adjective+noun) should peak as strongly as subword continuations.

The head fires only on tokenizer-split continuations and sentence-initial There+be, and every ordinary-prose crossing is spillover from those two triggers, so rare single-token bigrams such as fish|swam, open|wide and stops|there should stay below the line.
